title: The Wasteland's Merry Outlaw
description: Dialog nodes for Loxley, a charismatic wasteland thief who robs the rich caravans and distributes the spoils to squatter settlements. He dresses in pre-war camouflage with an absurdly maintained felt hat, speaks in an exaggerated mock-British accent, and insists he is fighting for a more equitable post-apocalypse.
backstory: Robin Loxley doesn't use his real name. What he'll tell you is that he was born in the NCR's most prosperous settlement, raised by a family of merchants, and that he watched his entire community sold in a land deal to a corporate caravan faction in 2275. He took what he could carry and walked into the wasteland with nothing but skills and a philosophy about redistribution. He robs the rich. He gives to the poor. He has an objectively magnificent hat.

intro.video_speech: Hail! I am Loxley — wealth redistribution specialist. The Crimson Caravan grows fat while the squatter camps starve. The maths are simple.
intro.text:
Hail, good traveller! I am Loxley — Robin of Loxley, if you prefer the full verse of it.

Some call us thieves. We prefer 'wealth redistribution specialists.'

The Crimson Caravan passes through this stretch twice a month. Fat shipments. Brahmin-bowed under the weight of it. And the folk in the squatter camps along the Mojave? Starving.

The maths are simple. Even the post-apocalypse can do the maths.

knowledge_nodes.text:
The Captain at the Dam? Yes, he's had us in his sights before.

We move faster than his patrols. The Merry Men are nothing if not fleet-footed.

He is not wrong to pursue us. He simply lacks the proper cause.

The Scavenger Queen? Brilliant woman.

We have a mutual arrangement — I don't rob her caravans; she doesn't tell the Dam where we camp.

A satisfying detente.

The abiding one? Yes, I've shared a fire with him.

A man of deep philosophical conviction and almost heroic passivity.

He gave me a bottle of something warm and told me the Wasteland abides. I found that... oddly useful.

You have met Arnold Black? A formidable individual.

He accompanied us on one redistribution. The Merry Men were very quiet afterward.

He said something about being back, then simply... left. We believed him.

Ah, the little orange-hooded one.

He wandered into our camp bleeding from something he could not name and left the next morning on a mule that wasn't his.

We were genuinely unsure if we should be worried or impressed.

emotional_nodes.text:
You look like one of the folk I rob *for*, not *from*.

Here. Take these. Consider it a redistribution in your favour.

My, my.

You are rather... prosperous for a wanderer.

You needn't worry. I only take from those who take from others first. But I am watching your accounting very closely.

quest_nodes.video_speech: A Crimson Caravan shipment hits Nipton Road in two days — medical supplies meant for a hoarder named Harwick. Help us redirect it to those who actually need it.
quest_nodes.text:
A Crimson Caravan shipment is coming through Nipton Road in two days' time.

Medical supplies, grain, water chips. Enough for three settlements. All of it bound for a fortified estate outside of Primm — a man named Harwick who charges triple for anything he doesn't simply hoard.

I need someone who can ride point. My Merry Men are... enthusiastic, but subtlety is not their shield.

Help us stop the caravan, separate the goods, and see them to Freeside and the squatter camps along Route 15. No killing unless they shoot first.

Harwick will be furious. I find I sleep very well despite that.

wildcards.text:
We prefer 'liberating undervalued resources from those with excessive surplus.'

But yes. In the old world's tongue — thieving. Quite good at it.

Little John is seven feet tall and afraid of scorpions. Friar Tuck eats twice his weight and quotes pre-war scripture at gunpoint. Maid Marion runs our intelligence network and has better aim than any of us.

Merry? Perhaps not always. But ours.

Ah, you noticed.

Pre-war Europe was not entirely glassed. Some culture survived the fires.

Mine is mostly affected, I'll confess. But it helps the legend.

The Sheriff of Nottingham, in my experience, is whoever controls the local water supply and the heaviest calibre weapon.

Out here, that rotates roughly every season.

The hat is non-negotiable.

It has survived two deathclaw attacks, a radstorm, and a casino bouncer in Freeside.

The hat stays.

Crimson Caravan prices their water at four caps the bottle in a drought.

In a settlement with twelve children and a broken well.

I find their redistribution ethic unconvincing.

fallback.video_speech: A merry day to you, traveller. Watch your pockets on the Nipton Road — though if you need what's in them, find me.
fallback.text:
A merry day to you, traveller.

Watch your pockets on the Nipton Road — though if you need what's in them, do come find me.
